items.stem: Which statement describes a reaction at dynamic equilibrium?
options: the concentrations of reactants and products are equal
the forward and reverse reactions have stopped
the reaction has gone to completion
the rates of the forward and reverse reactions are equal
items.answer: the rates of the forward and reverse reactions are equal
items.markingKey: Dynamic: both reactions continue at the same rate; concentrations stay constant (closed system).

items.stem: Explain why the concentrations of reactants and products remain constant at dynamic equilibrium even though reactions are still occurring.
items.answer: Forward and reverse reactions occur at the same rate, so each substance is formed as fast as it is used up.
items.markingKey: both reactions continue [1]; equal rates so no net change [1]

items.stem: Explain why adding more reactant moves the position of equilibrium to the right.
items.answer: The system opposes the increase in reactant concentration by using some of it up, so the forward reaction is favoured until equilibrium is re-established.
items.markingKey: opposes the change [1]; forward reaction uses up reactant [1]

items.stem: Ana sets up the equilibrium Fe³⁺(aq) (yellow) + SCN⁻(aq) ⇌ [FeSCN]²⁺(aq) (blood red). Describe and explain the colour change seen when more potassium thiocyanate solution is added.
items.answer: Deeper red: equilibrium moves right.
items.markingKey: colour change [1]; direction of shift [1]

items.stem: Amara sets up the equilibrium Cr₂O₇²⁻(aq) (orange) + H₂O(l) ⇌ 2CrO₄²⁻(aq) (yellow) + 2H⁺(aq). Describe and explain the colour change seen when aqueous sodium hydroxide is added.
items.answer: Turns yellow: OH⁻ removes H⁺, equilibrium moves right.
items.markingKey: colour change [1]; direction of shift [1]; reason using Le Chatelier’s principle [1]

items.stem: The equilibrium CO(g) + H₂O(g) ⇌ CO₂(g) + H₂(g), ΔH = −41 kJ mol⁻¹, is used in the water–gas shift reaction. (a) State Le Chatelier's principle. (b) Predict and explain the effect of increasing the temperature on the equilibrium yield. (c) State which change, if any, would alter the value of Kc.
items.answer: (a) If a change is made to a system at equilibrium, the position moves to minimise/oppose the change. (b) moves to the left: the forward reaction is exothermic; increasing temperature favours the endothermic direction to absorb heat (c) Only a change in temperature.
items.markingKey: (a) If a change is made to a system at equilibrium, the position moves to minimise/oppose the change. [1] (b) moves to the left: the forward reaction is exothermic; increasing temperature favours the endothermic direction to absorb heat [2] (c) Only a change in temperature. [1]

items.stem: What does Le Chatelier's principle state?
options: if a change is made to a system at equilibrium, the position of equilibrium moves to minimise the change
the equilibrium constant changes with concentration
equilibrium is reached only at high temperature
a catalyst moves the position of equilibrium to the right
items.answer: if a change is made to a system at equilibrium, the position of equilibrium moves to minimise the change
items.markingKey: The system opposes the imposed change.

items.stem: Explain the effect of adding hydrochloric acid to the equilibrium Cr₂O₇²⁻(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ 2CrO₄²⁻(aq) + 2H⁺(aq).
items.answer: Increased [H⁺] moves the equilibrium to the left to remove H⁺, so the solution becomes orange (more dichromate).
items.markingKey: moves left [1]; orange colour/opposes increase in H⁺ [1]

items.stem: Explain why the position of equilibrium in H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g) is not affected by pressure.
items.answer: There are 2 moles of gas on each side, so changing pressure does not favour either side.
items.markingKey: equal moles of gas [1]; neither side favoured [1]

items.stem: Ines writes in a revision note: "At equilibrium the concentrations of reactants and products are equal." Identify the error in this statement and give the correct version.
items.answer: The statement is incorrect. At equilibrium the concentrations are constant, not necessarily equal; the rates of forward and reverse reactions are equal.
items.markingKey: identifies the error [1]; correct chemistry stated with reason [1]

items.stem: Leila sets up the equilibrium Cr₂O₇²⁻(aq) (orange) + H₂O(l) ⇌ 2CrO₄²⁻(aq) (yellow) + 2H⁺(aq). Describe and explain the colour change seen when dilute sulfuric acid is added.
items.answer: Turns orange: increased [H⁺] moves equilibrium left.
items.markingKey: colour change [1]; direction of shift [1]

items.stem: Daniel investigates the equilibrium CH₄(g) + H₂O(g) ⇌ CO(g) + 3H₂(g) (ΔH = +206 kJ mol⁻¹) in a research laboratory. (a) State two features of a dynamic equilibrium. (b) State Le Chatelier's principle.
items.answer: (a) Rates of forward and reverse reactions equal; concentrations constant; closed system. (b) If a change is made to a system at equilibrium, the position moves to minimise/oppose the change.
items.markingKey: (a) Rates of forward and reverse reactions equal; concentrations constant; closed system. [2] (b) If a change is made to a system at equilibrium, the position moves to minimise/oppose the change. [1]

items.stem: The equilibrium CO(g) + 2H₂(g) ⇌ CH₃OH(g), ΔH = −91 kJ mol⁻¹, is used in methanol manufacture. (a) State two features of a dynamic equilibrium. (b) Predict and explain the effect of increasing the temperature on the equilibrium yield.
items.answer: (a) Rates of forward and reverse reactions equal; concentrations constant; closed system. (b) moves to the left: the forward reaction is exothermic; increasing temperature favours the endothermic direction to absorb heat
items.markingKey: (a) Rates of forward and reverse reactions equal; concentrations constant; closed system. [2] (b) moves to the left: the forward reaction is exothermic; increasing temperature favours the endothermic direction to absorb heat [2]

items.stem: Mateo investigates the equilibrium CH₄(g) + H₂O(g) ⇌ CO(g) + 3H₂(g) (ΔH = +206 kJ mol⁻¹) in an AS practical class. (a) State two features of a dynamic equilibrium. (b) Predict and explain the effect of increasing the pressure on the equilibrium yield. (c) State which change, if any, would alter the value of Kc.
items.answer: (a) Rates of forward and reverse reactions equal; concentrations constant; closed system. (b) moves to the left: there are 2 mol of gas on the left and 4 on the right; increasing pressure favours the side with fewer gas molecules (c) Only a change in temperature.
items.markingKey: (a) Rates of forward and reverse reactions equal; concentrations constant; closed system. [2] (b) moves to the left: there are 2 mol of gas on the left and 4 on the right; increasing pressure favours the side with fewer gas molecules [2] (c) Only a change in temperature. [1]

items.stem: What is the partial pressure of a gas in a mixture?
options: mole fraction of the gas × total pressure
the pressure the gas exerts at r.t.p.
items.answer: mole fraction of the gas × total pressure
items.markingKey: p(A) = x(A) × P(total); the sum of partial pressures = total pressure.

items.stem: Explain why increasing the pressure on N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ increases the yield of NH₃ but does not change Kp.
items.answer: Kp depends only on temperature; when pressure increases the ratio of partial pressures temporarily differs from Kp and the equilibrium shifts right until the ratio again equals Kp.
items.markingKey: Kp depends only on temperature [1]; position shifts to restore ratio [1]

items.stem: Explain why the volume of the container is not needed to calculate Kc for H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI.
items.answer: The total moles on each side are equal, so the volume terms cancel in the Kc expression.
items.markingKey: equal powers top and bottom [1]; V cancels [1]

items.stem: At equilibrium at a certain temperature, [N₂] = 0.50 mol dm⁻³, [H₂] = 2.00 mol dm⁻³ and [NH₃] = 0.25 mol dm⁻³ for N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g). Calculate Kc and give its units.
items.answer: 0.0156 mol⁻² dm⁶

items.stem: 2.00 mol of hydrogen and 0.50 mol of iodine are heated in a sealed container until equilibrium is reached: H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g). At equilibrium 0.750 mol of HI is present. Calculate Kc.
items.answer: Kc = 2.77 (no units)

items.stem: At equilibrium at a certain temperature, [N₂] = 0.50 mol dm⁻³, [H₂] = 3.00 mol dm⁻³ and [NH₃] = 0.20 mol dm⁻³ for N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g). Calculate Kc and give its units.
items.answer: 0.00296 mol⁻² dm⁶

items.stem: Diego mixes 2.00 mol of ethanoic acid and 1.00 mol of ethanol with a little concentrated H₂SO₄ and leaves the mixture to reach equilibrium at room temperature. 0.667 mol of ethyl ethanoate is formed. (a) Calculate Kc and explain why it has no units. (b) Describe how the amount of ethanoic acid at equilibrium could be found.
items.answer: (a) 1.00; volume and concentration units cancel (equal moles each side) (b) Titrate a sample with standard NaOH (subtracting the H₂SO₄ catalyst contribution), quickly / after diluting in ice-cold water to stop reaction.
items.markingKey: (a) 1.00; volume and concentration units cancel (equal moles each side) [2] (b) Titrate a sample with standard NaOH (subtracting the H₂SO₄ catalyst contribution), quickly / after diluting in ice-cold water to stop reaction. [2]

items.stem: In a college laboratory in Mumbai, an ester equilibrium is set up from 2.00 mol CH₃COOH and 1.00 mol C₂H₅OH; at equilibrium 0.667 mol of CH₃COOC₂H₅ is present. (a) Write an expression for Kc. (b) Calculate Kc and explain why it has no units. (c) Describe how the amount of ethanoic acid at equilibrium could be found.
items.answer: (a) [CH₃COOC₂H₅][H₂O] / [CH₃COOH][C₂H₅OH] (b) 1.00; volume and concentration units cancel (equal moles each side) (c) Titrate a sample with standard NaOH (subtracting the H₂SO₄ catalyst contribution), quickly / after diluting in ice-cold water to stop reaction.
items.markingKey: (a) [CH₃COOC₂H₅][H₂O] / [CH₃COOH][C₂H₅OH] [1] (b) 1.00; volume and concentration units cancel (equal moles each side) [2] (c) Titrate a sample with standard NaOH (subtracting the H₂SO₄ catalyst contribution), quickly / after diluting in ice-cold water to stop reaction. [2]

items.stem: What does a very large value of Kc indicate?
options: the position lies far to the left
the position of equilibrium lies far to the right
items.answer: the position of equilibrium lies far to the right
items.markingKey: Large K: mostly products at equilibrium.

items.stem: For an exothermic reaction, what happens to Kc when temperature is increased?
items.answer: it decreases
items.markingKey: Equilibrium shifts left (endothermic direction) so K decreases.

items.stem: Explain why water is included in the Kc expression for esterification but not for reactions in dilute aqueous solution.
items.answer: In esterification water is a product present in small amounts and its concentration changes; in dilute aqueous solution water is in huge excess and its concentration is effectively constant.
items.markingKey: water concentration changes in esterification [1]; constant in dilute solution [1]

items.stem: A student in Bangkok claims that a partial pressure is the number of moles of a gas multiplied by the total pressure. Is the student correct? Explain your answer.
items.answer: The statement is incorrect. Partial pressure = mole fraction × total pressure.
items.markingKey: identifies the error [1]; correct chemistry stated with reason [1]

items.stem: A student in Bangkok claims that for N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, Kc = [NH₃]/[N₂][H₂]. Is the student correct? Explain your answer.
items.answer: The statement is incorrect. Concentrations are raised to the power of their coefficients: Kc = [NH₃]²/[N₂][H₂]³.
items.markingKey: identifies the error [1]; correct chemistry stated with reason [1]

items.stem: What are the units of Kc for N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g)?
items.answer: mol⁻² dm⁶
items.markingKey: Kc = [NH₃]² / [N₂][H₂]³: units mol⁻² dm⁶.

items.stem: At equilibrium at a certain temperature, [N₂] = 0.80 mol dm⁻³, [H₂] = 3.00 mol dm⁻³ and [NH₃] = 0.20 mol dm⁻³ for N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g). Calculate Kc and give its units.
items.answer: 0.00185 mol⁻² dm⁶

items.stem: 0.500 mol of PCl₅ is heated in a sealed 1.00 dm³ flask. At equilibrium 60% has dissociated: PCl₅(g) ⇌ PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g). Calculate Kc, giving its units.
items.answer: 0.450 mol dm⁻³
items.markingKey: n(PCl₃) = n(Cl₂) = 0.300 mol, n(PCl₅) = 0.200 mol [1]; concentrations ÷ 1.00 dm³ [1]; Kc = 0.450 [1]; mol dm⁻³ [1]

items.stem: At equilibrium at a certain temperature, [N₂] = 0.80 mol dm⁻³, [H₂] = 3.00 mol dm⁻³ and [NH₃] = 0.25 mol dm⁻³ for N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g). Calculate Kc and give its units.
items.answer: 0.00289 mol⁻² dm⁶

items.stem: Jonas mixes 2.00 mol of ethanoic acid and 1.50 mol of ethanol with a little concentrated H₂SO₄ and leaves the mixture to reach equilibrium at room temperature. 1.001 mol of ethyl ethanoate is formed. (a) Write an expression for Kc. (b) Calculate Kc and explain why it has no units.
items.answer: (a) [CH₃COOC₂H₅][H₂O] / [CH₃COOH][C₂H₅OH] (b) 2.01; volume and concentration units cancel (equal moles each side)
items.markingKey: (a) [CH₃COOC₂H₅][H₂O] / [CH₃COOH][C₂H₅OH] [1] (b) 2.01; volume and concentration units cancel (equal moles each side) [2]

items.stem: Ana mixes 1.00 mol of ethanoic acid and 1.50 mol of ethanol with a little concentrated H₂SO₄ and leaves the mixture to reach equilibrium at room temperature. 0.667 mol of ethyl ethanoate is formed. (a) Write an expression for Kc. (b) Calculate the amounts of all four substances at equilibrium.
items.answer: (a) [CH₃COOC₂H₅][H₂O] / [CH₃COOH][C₂H₅OH] (b) acid 0.333, ethanol 0.833, ester 0.667, water 0.667 mol
items.markingKey: (a) [CH₃COOC₂H₅][H₂O] / [CH₃COOH][C₂H₅OH] [1] (b) acid 0.333, ethanol 0.833, ester 0.667, water 0.667 mol [2]

items.stem: What catalyst is used in the Haber process?
items.answer: iron
items.markingKey: Finely divided iron (with promoters).

items.stem: Explain why a temperature of about 450 °C is used in the Haber process even though a lower temperature gives a higher equilibrium yield.
items.answer: The forward reaction is exothermic so low temperature favours ammonia, but the rate would be too slow; 450 °C is a compromise giving acceptable rate and yield.
items.markingKey: low T higher yield (exothermic) [1]; rate too slow at low T, compromise [1]

items.stem: Explain why a very high pressure is not used in the Haber process.
items.answer: High pressure increases yield and rate but is expensive (energy to compress gas, strong pipes) and dangerous.
items.markingKey: yield would increase [1]; cost/safety [1]

items.stem: In one pass through the reactor of an ammonia plant in Cairo, 25% of the nitrogen is converted into ammonia. Calculate the mass of ammonia, in tonnes, made from 100 tonnes of nitrogen in one pass. (N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃)
items.answer: 30.4 tonnes

items.stem: A sulfuric acid plant burns 10 tonnes of sulfur. Overall conversion of sulfur into H₂SO₄ is 99.5%. Calculate the mass of sulfuric acid produced. (S → SO₂ → SO₃ → H₂SO₄)
items.answer: 30.4 tonnes

items.stem: A chemical company in Muscat operates the Contact process. (a) State the conditions used for this step. (b) Describe how SO₃ is converted into sulfuric acid.
items.answer: (a) About 450 °C, 100–200 kPa, V₂O₅ catalyst. (b) Absorbed in concentrated H₂SO₄ to give oleum, H₂S₂O₇, then diluted with water.
items.markingKey: (a) About 450 °C, 100–200 kPa, V₂O₅ catalyst. [2] (b) Absorbed in concentrated H₂SO₄ to give oleum, H₂S₂O₇, then diluted with water. [2]

items.stem: What catalyst is used in the Contact process?
items.answer: vanadium(V) oxide, V₂O₅
items.markingKey: V₂O₅ catalyses 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃.

items.stem: Explain why the unreacted gases are recycled in the Haber process.
items.answer: Only about 15% conversion per pass; recycling the N₂ and H₂ means almost all is eventually converted, reducing waste and cost.
items.markingKey: low conversion per pass [1]; overall conversion high, saves cost [1]

items.stem: Explain why SO₃ is absorbed in concentrated sulfuric acid rather than water in the Contact process.
items.answer: SO₃ reacts violently with water, forming a mist of acid; dissolving in concentrated H₂SO₄ gives oleum, H₂S₂O₇, which is diluted carefully.
items.markingKey: violent reaction/mist with water [1]; forms oleum then diluted [1]

items.stem: In a test answer, Leila states: "In the Haber process the temperature is raised to 450 °C to increase the yield." Explain why this statement is incorrect.
items.answer: The statement is incorrect. Raising temperature decreases the yield (exothermic); 450 °C is used for an acceptable rate.
items.markingKey: identifies the error [1]; correct chemistry stated with reason [1]

items.stem: A sulfuric acid plant burns 5 tonnes of sulfur. Overall conversion of sulfur into H₂SO₄ is 99.5%. Calculate the mass of sulfuric acid produced. (S → SO₂ → SO₃ → H₂SO₄)
items.answer: 15.2 tonnes

items.stem: Ines is preparing a report on the Contact process for a class in Lisbon. (a) Write the equation for the equilibrium step, with state symbols. (b) Write the expression for Kp.
items.answer: (a) 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g), ΔH = −197 kJ mol⁻¹ (b) Kp = p(SO₃)² / p(SO₂)² p(O₂)
items.markingKey: (a) 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g), ΔH = −197 kJ mol⁻¹ [2] (b) Kp = p(SO₃)² / p(SO₂)² p(O₂) [1]

items.stem: A chemical company in Dhaka operates the Contact process. (a) Explain why the temperature is a compromise. (b) Describe how SO₃ is converted into sulfuric acid.
items.answer: (a) Exothermic: low T higher yield but slower rate. (b) Absorbed in concentrated H₂SO₄ to give oleum, H₂S₂O₇, then diluted with water.
items.markingKey: (a) Exothermic: low T higher yield but slower rate. [2] (b) Absorbed in concentrated H₂SO₄ to give oleum, H₂S₂O₇, then diluted with water. [2]

items.stem: A chemical company in Istanbul operates the Haber process. (a) Explain why the temperature used is a compromise. (b) Write the expression for Kp. (c) Describe how ammonia is separated and what happens to unreacted gases.
items.answer: (a) Lower T gives higher yield (exothermic) but slower rate; 450 °C balances these. (b) Kp = p(NH₃)² / p(N₂) p(H₂)³ (c) Cooled to liquefy NH₃; N₂ and H₂ recycled.
items.markingKey: (a) Lower T gives higher yield (exothermic) but slower rate; 450 °C balances these. [2] (b) Kp = p(NH₃)² / p(N₂) p(H₂)³ [1] (c) Cooled to liquefy NH₃; N₂ and H₂ recycled. [2]

items.stem: What is a Brønsted–Lowry acid?
options: a substance that produces OH⁻ ions
items.answer: a proton (H⁺) donor
items.markingKey: Acid donates H⁺; base accepts H⁺.

items.stem: Explain the difference between a strong acid and a concentrated acid.
items.answer: Strong refers to complete ionisation in water; concentrated refers to a large amount of acid per dm³ of solution. A weak acid can be concentrated.
items.markingKey: strong = fully ionised [1]; concentrated = amount per volume [1]

items.stem: Describe an experiment to show that ethanoic acid is weaker than hydrochloric acid of the same concentration.
items.answer: Measure pH (ethanoic higher), compare electrical conductivity (lower), or rate of reaction with magnesium (slower bubbling) for equal concentrations.
items.markingKey: valid method [1]; correct result for weak acid [1]

items.stem: For the reaction HSO₄⁻ + H₂O ⇌ SO₄²⁻ + H₃O⁺, identify the Brønsted–Lowry acid and base on the left-hand side and give the two conjugate acid–base pairs.
items.answer: acid HSO₄⁻, base H₂O; pairs: HSO₄⁻/SO₄²⁻ and H₃O⁺/H₂O
items.markingKey: acid HSO₄⁻, base H₂O [1]; one conjugate pair correct [1]

items.stem: For the reaction HCl + NH₃ → NH₄⁺ + Cl⁻, identify the Brønsted–Lowry acid and base on the left-hand side and give the two conjugate acid–base pairs.
items.answer: acid HCl, base NH₃; pairs: HCl/Cl⁻ and NH₄⁺/NH₃
items.markingKey: acid HCl and base NH₃ [1]; pair HCl/Cl⁻ [1]; pair NH₄⁺/NH₃ [1]

items.stem: Omar compares 0.100 mol dm⁻³ methanoic acid with 0.100 mol dm⁻³ hydrochloric acid in a quality-control laboratory. (a) Write an equation to show that methanoic acid is a weak acid. (b) Identify the conjugate base of methanoic acid. (c) Suggest a suitable indicator for titrating the weak acid with NaOH and explain your choice.
items.answer: (a) HCOOH ⇌ HCOO⁻ + H⁺ (b) HCOO⁻ (c) Phenolphthalein: equivalence point pH > 7 (about 8–9) within its range.
items.markingKey: (a) HCOOH ⇌ HCOO⁻ + H⁺ [1] (b) HCOO⁻ [1] (c) Phenolphthalein: equivalence point pH > 7 (about 8–9) within its range. [2]

items.stem: Which statement about carbonic acid is correct?
options: it does not ionise in water at all
it is a strong acid, fully ionised in water
it is a weak acid, only partially ionised in water
items.answer: it is a weak acid, only partially ionised in water
items.markingKey: carbonic acid: weak acid.

items.stem: Explain why water can act as both an acid and a base.
items.answer: It can donate a proton (forming OH⁻) or accept a proton (forming H₃O⁺); it is amphoteric (amphiprotic).
items.markingKey: donates H⁺ [1]; accepts H⁺ [1]

items.stem: In the reaction HCOOH + H₂O ⇌ HCOO⁻ + H₃O⁺, which species acts as a Brønsted–Lowry acid (left to right)?
items.answer: HCOOH
items.markingKey: HCOOH donates a proton to H₂O.

items.stem: For the reaction HCl + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + Cl⁻, identify the Brønsted–Lowry acid and base on the left-hand side and give the two conjugate acid–base pairs.
items.answer: acid HCl, base H₂O; pairs: HCl/Cl⁻ and H₃O⁺/H₂O
items.markingKey: acid HCl, base H₂O [1]; one conjugate pair correct [1]

items.stem: For the reaction CH₃COOH + H₂O ⇌ CH₃COO⁻ + H₃O⁺, identify the Brønsted–Lowry acid and base on the left-hand side and give the two conjugate acid–base pairs.
items.answer: acid CH₃COOH, base H₂O; pairs: CH₃COOH/CH₃COO⁻ and H₃O⁺/H₂O
items.markingKey: acid CH₃COOH, base H₂O [1]; one conjugate pair correct [1]

items.stem: Elena compares 0.100 mol dm⁻³ propanoic acid with 0.100 mol dm⁻³ hydrochloric acid in a quality-control laboratory. (a) Define a Brønsted–Lowry acid. (b) Explain why both acids need the same volume of NaOH for neutralisation.
items.answer: (a) A proton donor. (b) Same amount of acid (monoprotic); weak acid equilibrium shifts as H⁺ is removed, until all reacts.
items.markingKey: (a) A proton donor. [1] (b) Same amount of acid (monoprotic); weak acid equilibrium shifts as H⁺ is removed, until all reacts. [2]

items.answer: (a) HCOOH ⇌ HCOO⁻ + H⁺ (b) HCOO⁻ (c) Same amount of acid (monoprotic); weak acid equilibrium shifts as H⁺ is removed, until all reacts. (d) Phenolphthalein: equivalence point pH > 7 (about 8–9) within its range.

items.stem: What condition is needed for a dynamic equilibrium to be established?
items.answer: a closed system

items.stem: A student in Hanoi claims that adding a catalyst increases the yield at equilibrium. Is the student correct? Explain your answer.
items.answer: The statement is incorrect. A catalyst increases the rates of both reactions equally; the position of equilibrium and the yield are unchanged.
items.markingKey: identifies the error [1]; correct chemistry stated with reason [1]

items.stem: Ethan sets up the equilibrium N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g), ΔH = +58 kJ mol⁻¹ (N₂O₄ colourless, NO₂ brown). Describe and explain the colour change seen when the syringe is placed in hot water.
items.answer: Darker brown: endothermic forward reaction favoured, more NO₂.
items.markingKey: colour change [1]; direction of shift [1]

items.answer: Paler red/yellow: equilibrium moves left to replace Fe³⁺.

[2] (b) If a change is made to a system at equilibrium, the position moves to minimise/oppose the change. items.stem: Which substances are omitted from a Kc expression for a heterogeneous equilibrium?
items.answer: pure solids (and pure liquids)
items.markingKey: Their concentrations are constant.

items.stem: Kwame writes in a revision note: "Adding more nitrogen to the Haber equilibrium increases Kc." Identify the error in this statement and give the correct version.
items.answer: The statement is incorrect. Kc is unchanged; only temperature alters K. The position shifts right.
items.markingKey: identifies the error [1]; correct chemistry stated with reason [1]

items.stem: A research chemist in Doha measures equilibrium compositions of gas mixtures. (a) Explain why increasing the pressure on N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ increases the yield of NH₃ but does not change Kp. (b) Explain why the volume of the container is not needed to calculate Kc for H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI.
items.answer: (a) Kp depends only on temperature; when pressure increases the ratio of partial pressures temporarily differs from Kp and the equilibrium shifts right until the ratio again equals Kp. (b) The total moles on each side are equal, so the volume terms cancel in the Kc expression.
items.markingKey: (a) Kp depends only on temperature; position shifts to restore ratio [2] (b) equal powers top and bottom; V cancels [2]

items.stem: Arjun mixes 2.00 mol of ethanoic acid with 0.50 mol of ethanol and a few drops of concentrated sulfuric acid. At equilibrium the mixture contains 0.335 mol of ethyl ethanoate. Calculate Kc for CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O.
items.markingKey: equilibrium: acid 1.665, ethanol 0.165, ester 0.335, water 0.335 mol [1]; Kc expression [1]; Kc = 0.408, no units [1]

items.stem: 0.400 mol of PCl₅ is heated in a sealed 2.00 dm³ flask. At equilibrium 25% has dissociated: PCl₅(g) ⇌ PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g). Calculate Kc, giving its units.
items.answer: 0.0167 mol dm⁻³
items.markingKey: n(PCl₃) = n(Cl₂) = 0.100 mol, n(PCl₅) = 0.300 mol [1]; concentrations ÷ 2.00 dm³ [1]; Kc = 0.0167 [1]; mol dm⁻³ [1]

items.stem: Samuel mixes 2.00 mol of ethanoic acid and 1.00 mol of ethanol with a little concentrated H₂SO₄ and leaves the mixture to reach equilibrium at room temperature. 0.667 mol of ethyl ethanoate is formed. (a) Calculate the amounts of all four substances at equilibrium. (b) Describe how the amount of ethanoic acid at equilibrium could be found.
items.answer: (a) acid 1.333, ethanol 0.333, ester 0.667, water 0.667 mol (b) Titrate a sample with standard NaOH (subtracting the H₂SO₄ catalyst contribution), quickly / after diluting in ice-cold water to stop reaction.
items.markingKey: (a) acid 1.333, ethanol 0.333, ester 0.667, water 0.667 mol [2] (b) Titrate a sample with standard NaOH (subtracting the H₂SO₄ catalyst contribution), quickly / after diluting in ice-cold water to stop reaction. [2]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) State how ammonia is removed from the equilibrium mixture in the Haber process. (b) What typical temperature is used in the Contact process?
items.answer: (a) By cooling: ammonia liquefies and is removed; unreacted N₂ and H₂ are recycled. (b) about 450 °C
items.markingKey: (a) [1] (b) 400–450 °C: compromise between rate and yield.

items.stem: Lina writes in a revision note: "In the Haber process the temperature is raised to 450 °C to increase the yield." Identify the error in this statement and give the correct version.
items.answer: The statement is incorrect. Raising temperature decreases the yield (exothermic); 450 °C is used for an acceptable rate.
items.markingKey: identifies the error [1]; correct chemistry stated with reason [1]

items.stem: In one pass through the reactor of an ammonia plant in Colombo, 28% of the nitrogen is converted into ammonia. Calculate the mass of ammonia, in tonnes, made from 50 tonnes of nitrogen in one pass. (N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃)
items.answer: 17.0 tonnes

items.stem: A sulfuric acid plant burns 64 tonnes of sulfur. Overall conversion of sulfur into H₂SO₄ is 99.5%. Calculate the mass of sulfuric acid produced. (S → SO₂ → SO₃ → H₂SO₄)
items.answer: 195 tonnes

items.stem: Tariq is preparing a report on the Contact process for a class in Dubai. (a) Write the equation for the equilibrium step, with state symbols. (b) Explain why a high pressure is not used. (c) Explain why the temperature is a compromise.
items.answer: (a) 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g), ΔH = −197 kJ mol⁻¹ (b) Conversion is already >99% at low pressure; high pressure is costly. (c) Exothermic: low T higher yield but slower rate.
items.markingKey: (a) 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g), ΔH = −197 kJ mol⁻¹ [2] (b) Conversion is already >99% at low pressure; high pressure is costly. [2] (c) Exothermic: low T higher yield but slower rate. [2]

items.stem: Explain why methyl orange is not a suitable indicator for the titration of ethanoic acid with sodium hydroxide.
items.answer: The pH at the equivalence point is above 7 (about 8–9) and the vertical section is above methyl orange’s range (3–5), so it changes colour too early.
items.markingKey: equivalence above 7 [1]; methyl orange range too low [1]

items.stem: "In NH₃ + H₂O ⇌ NH₄⁺ + OH⁻, ammonia is the acid because it gains a hydrogen." Comment on this statement made by a student, correcting any error.
items.answer: The statement is incorrect. Ammonia accepts a proton, so it is the base; water donates the proton and is the acid.
items.markingKey: identifies the error [1]; correct chemistry stated with reason [1]

items.stem: For the reaction HCO₃⁻ + H₂O ⇌ CO₃²⁻ + H₃O⁺, identify the Brønsted–Lowry acid and base on the left-hand side and give the two conjugate acid–base pairs.
items.answer: acid HCO₃⁻, base H₂O; pairs: HCO₃⁻/CO₃²⁻ and H₃O⁺/H₂O
items.markingKey: acid HCO₃⁻, base H₂O [1]; one conjugate pair correct [1]

items.stem: Tariq compares 0.100 mol dm⁻³ methanoic acid with 0.100 mol dm⁻³ hydrochloric acid in a quality-control laboratory. (a) Write an equation to show that methanoic acid is a weak acid. (b) Identify the conjugate base of methanoic acid. (c) Explain why both acids need the same volume of NaOH for neutralisation.
items.answer: (a) HCOOH ⇌ HCOO⁻ + H⁺ (b) HCOO⁻ (c) Same amount of acid (monoprotic); weak acid equilibrium shifts as H⁺ is removed, until all reacts.
items.markingKey: (a) HCOOH ⇌ HCOO⁻ + H⁺ [1] (b) HCOO⁻ [1] (c) Same amount of acid (monoprotic); weak acid equilibrium shifts as H⁺ is removed, until all reacts. [2]

items.stem: Which change alters the value of the equilibrium constant Kc?
items.answer: changing the temperature
items.markingKey: Only temperature changes K; concentration and pressure changes shift position but not K.

items.stem: Ines studies reversible reactions in sealed containers in a research laboratory. Explain the effect of adding hydrochloric acid to the equilibrium Cr₂O₇²⁻(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ 2CrO₄²⁻(aq) + 2H⁺(aq).
items.answer: Increased [H⁺] moves the equilibrium to the left to remove H⁺, so the solution becomes orange (more dichromate).
items.markingKey: moves left; orange colour/opposes increase in H⁺ [2]

items.stem: Ines sets up the equilibrium N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g), ΔH = +58 kJ mol⁻¹ (N₂O₄ colourless, NO₂ brown). Describe and explain the colour change seen when the syringe plunger is pushed in (pressure increased) and held.
items.answer: After an initial darkening, the colour becomes paler: equilibrium moves left to fewer gas molecules.
items.markingKey: colour change [1]; direction of shift [1]

items.stem: The equilibrium CH₄(g) + H₂O(g) ⇌ CO(g) + 3H₂(g), ΔH = +206 kJ mol⁻¹, is used in steam reforming of methane. (a) Predict and explain the effect of increasing the temperature on the equilibrium yield. (b) State which change, if any, would alter the value of Kc.
items.answer: (a) moves to the right: the forward reaction is endothermic; increasing temperature favours the endothermic direction to absorb heat (b) Only a change in temperature.
items.markingKey: (a) moves to the right: the forward reaction is endothermic; increasing temperature favours the endothermic direction to absorb heat [2] (b) Only a change in temperature. [1]

items.stem: The equilibrium CH₄(g) + 2H₂S(g) ⇌ CS₂(g) + 4H₂(g), ΔH = +232 kJ mol⁻¹, is used in a laboratory study. (a) Predict and explain the effect of increasing the pressure on the equilibrium yield. (b) State and explain the effect of a catalyst. (c) State which change, if any, would alter the value of Kc.
items.answer: (a) moves to the left: there are 3 mol of gas on the left and 5 on the right; increasing pressure favours the side with fewer gas molecules (b) No change in position; equilibrium reached faster as both rates increase equally. (c) Only a change in temperature.
items.markingKey: (a) moves to the left: there are 3 mol of gas on the left and 5 on the right; increasing pressure favours the side with fewer gas molecules [2] (b) No change in position; equilibrium reached faster as both rates increase equally. [2] (c) Only a change in temperature. [1]

items.stem: What are the units of Kc for H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g)?
items.answer: no units
items.markingKey: mol² dm⁻⁶ / mol² dm⁻⁶: units cancel.

items.stem: Omar carries out equilibrium calculations for an AS test. Explain why the volume of the container is not needed to calculate Kc for H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI.
items.answer: The total moles on each side are equal, so the volume terms cancel in the Kc expression.
items.markingKey: equal powers top and bottom; V cancels [2]

items.stem: "A partial pressure is the number of moles of a gas multiplied by the total pressure." Comment on this statement made by a student, correcting any error.
items.answer: The statement is incorrect. Partial pressure = mole fraction × total pressure.
items.markingKey: identifies the error [1]; correct chemistry stated with reason [1]

items.stem: At equilibrium at a certain temperature, [N₂] = 0.80 mol dm⁻³, [H₂] = 1.50 mol dm⁻³ and [NH₃] = 0.30 mol dm⁻³ for N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g). Calculate Kc and give its units.
items.answer: 0.0333 mol⁻² dm⁶

items.stem: 0.200 mol of PCl₅ is heated in a sealed 2.00 dm³ flask. At equilibrium 40% has dissociated: PCl₅(g) ⇌ PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g). Calculate Kc, giving its units.
items.answer: 0.0267 mol dm⁻³

items.stem: In a research laboratory in Mumbai, an ester equilibrium is set up from 1.00 mol CH₃COOH and 1.00 mol C₂H₅OH; at equilibrium 0.667 mol of CH₃COOC₂H₅ is present. (a) Calculate Kc and explain why it has no units. (b) State the role of the concentrated sulfuric acid and its effect on the equilibrium position.
items.answer: (a) 4.01; volume and concentration units cancel (equal moles each side) (b) Catalyst: equilibrium reached faster, position unchanged.

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) What catalyst is used in the Haber process? (b) State how ammonia is removed from the equilibrium mixture in the Haber process.
items.answer: (a) iron (b) By cooling: ammonia liquefies and is removed; unreacted N₂ and H₂ are recycled.

items.stem: Elena researches how sulfuric acid is made industrially. Explain why SO₃ is absorbed in concentrated sulfuric acid rather than water in the Contact process.
items.answer: SO₃ reacts violently with water, forming a mist of acid; dissolving in concentrated H₂SO₄ gives oleum, H₂S₂O₇, which is diluted carefully.
items.markingKey: violent reaction/mist with water; forms oleum then diluted [2]

items.stem: In one pass through the reactor of an ammonia plant in Mumbai, 20% of the nitrogen is converted into ammonia. Calculate the mass of ammonia, in tonnes, made from 20 tonnes of nitrogen in one pass. (N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃)
items.answer: 4.86 tonnes

items.stem: Omar is preparing a report on the Contact process for a class in Kathmandu. (a) Explain why the temperature is a compromise. (b) Write the expression for Kp.
items.answer: (a) Exothermic: low T higher yield but slower rate. (b) Kp = p(SO₃)² / p(SO₂)² p(O₂)

items.stem: Nadia is preparing a report on the Haber process for a class in Karachi. (a) Write the equation for the reaction, with state symbols, and give the sign of ΔH. (b) State the typical conditions used. (c) Explain the choice of pressure.
items.answer: (a) N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g); ΔH negative (−92 kJ mol⁻¹) (b) About 450 °C, 20 000 kPa (200 atm), iron catalyst. (c) High pressure favours fewer gas moles (product) and increases rate; very high pressure too costly/dangerous.

items.stem: Tomás writes in a revision note: "A weak acid is a dilute acid." Identify the error in this statement and give the correct version.
